# Problem 1

## Writing Birthday Function

```{r writing_function, message = F}
# writing birthday function 
duplicate_birthdays = function(n) {
  
  # drawing “birthdays” for each person randomly
  birthdays = sample(1:365, n, replace = TRUE)

  # checking for duplicate birthdays
  duplicate_birthdays = length(unique(birthdays)) < n
  
  # returning duplicate birthdays
  return(duplicate_birthdays)
}
```

## Running Simulations

```{r simulating_function, message = F}
# simulating function and computing prob. that <= 2 people will share a birthday
birthday_probabilities_df =
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    duplicates = map_lgl(number_of_people, duplicate_birthdays) 
  ) |>
   group_by(number_of_people) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(duplicates)
  ) |>
  print()
```

## Plotting Probabilities

```{r plotting_probabilies, message = F}
# making a plot showing the probability as a function of group size
birthday_probabilities_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = probability)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of Duplicate Birthdays",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of Duplicate Birthday"
  )
```

## Commenting on the Results

The `birthday_probabilities_df` plot shows that as group size increases so does the probability of duplicate birthdays, assuming each person is randomly assigned a birthday. Looking at the *Probability of Duplicate Birthdays* plot, this increase is initially gradual, but becomes much steeper as group size grows. As the group size approaches 50, the probability of at least one duplicate birthday approaches 1.00. At group size 23, this probability is already approximately 0.50.


# Problem 2

## Creating the Data Frame

```{r creating_dataframe, message = F}
# creating the data frame containing all file names
participants_df =
  participant_files =
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
  print()
```

## Adding Participant Data to the Dataframe

```{r filling_dataframe, message = F}
# iterating over file names and read in data for each subject 
participants_df = 
  participants_df |>   
  mutate(
     data = map(path,read_csv)
  ) |>
  unnest(data) |>
  print()
```

## Tidying the result

```{r tidying_dataframe, message = F}
# manipulating file names to include control arm and subject ID; general tidying
participants_df =
  participants_df |>
  mutate(
    subject_id = str_replace(files, "\\.csv$", ""),
    arm = case_when(
      str_starts(subject_id, "con") ~ "Control",
      str_starts(subject_id, "cov") ~ "Control",
      str_starts(subject_id, "exp") ~ "Experimental"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    week = as.numeric(str_remove(week, "week_"))
  ) |>
  select(subject_id, arm, week, observation) |>
  print()
```
